Geometry contribution (three dominant ancestral species)
Picking a source switches on the skeleton overlay in the main viewport. The result skeleton is blended joint-by-joint from the same three species and weights, in a separate pass from the vertex blend. Only rest-pose joint positions are blended (see notes below).
SPECIMEN SHELF
Choose a base and a secondary. Each strip is that creature's 48-slot ancestry.
What is real, what is approximated. Everything shown is computed live by the same code path used when you press “Merge & keep”: exact 32/16 index-selected ancestry transfer, top-three species by frequency (ties → lower id), vertex-by-vertex weighted interpolation over one shared master mesh, secondary-parent skin, palette hue rotation that leaves greys alone, OR-inheritance of body-part flags, and ground correction after blending. Approximations / unverified: the five-element compass (Water › Fire › Air › Lightning › Earth › Water; blue, red, white, yellow, green) and its angle→hue mapping, with Air paling a skin, the element inheritance rule (32/16 blend, kept separate from visual ancestry), skeleton blending of rest-pose joint positions with a procedural retargeted animation (frequency ∝ √leg length; the exact original animation evaluation is unverified, so the base parent's family drives the clip and the secondary only optionally mixes amplitudes), and the ground “foot marker” (lowest support point). All are single constants in CONFIG. The 216 species (about 15.9k vertices, 76 anatomical parts each) are original designs, each with its own authored proportions, gear, palette, skin pattern and markings. They are parametric sculpts on one shared master topology (tube sections with superellipse profiles), not hand-modelled meshes.
